ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is the graph of the function f, the horizontal axis is labeled x=1,2,3,4, and the vertical axis is labeled y=2,4. The curve touches the horizontal axis at x=3, that is, f(3)=0; at x=4, the height of the curve is about 2, so from the graph it is read that f(4)=2. Reasoning: The problem gives g(x)=∫_0^{x^2} f(t) dt. Let G(u)=∫_0^u f(t)dt, then g(x)=G(x^2). By the fundamental theorem of calculus and the chain rule, g'(x)=G'(x^2)·2x=f(x^2)·2x. Substituting x=2, obtain g'(2)=f(4)·4. From the graph f(4)=2, so g'(2)=4·2=8.
